results.content:
According to recent polling averages, Democrats lead Republicans by 6 to 7 points on the generic congressional ballot as of late August 2026. An Emerson College poll released in mid-August showed 51% support for Democratic candidates compared to 43% for Republicans, with 6% undecided. Ballotpedia’s polling index as of August 26 put Democrats ahead by 7 points, while Nate Silver’s tracking showed a Democratic margin of 6.6 points. results.content: This lead marks an improvement for Democrats, whose edge had ebbed to only around 4 points in July. But since the conflict with Iran heated up again and the price of gas rose, the Democrats’ have tended to have a larger advantage in surveys testing 2026 preferences. It’s no surprise that military operations against Iran and rising gas prices have hurt the president’s party at a time when concerns about the cost of living and disapproval of President Trump’s handling of the economy are high.
